cases.why: the state this item added, dropped from the handler. The markup still says All Games is pressed, so the page loads right and every static check passes; after one click the highlighted chip and the one a screen reader calls pressed are different chips, which is worse than no state at all.

Model Lab's chips return to the convention they had before: aria-current says 'this is the current item in a set of links', which is not what a filter toggle is, and leaves the page with two ways of saying the same thing.
a filter chip added or copied without the attribute: it looks exactly like its neighbours and is silent to a screen reader until the first click, and only then if the handler reaches it.

the trap this item walked into and back out of. Before, only series toggles carried aria-pressed, so a bare .btn-chip[aria-pressed="false"] rule was safe; now every unchosen filter chip carries it too, and that rule turns Model Disagreement and Flagged Only dashed on page load. Nothing throws and the tests about state all pass.
